verdict.rationale: LangSmith publishes a full OpenAPI 3.1 spec for 'programmatically create and manage LangSmith resources', with a live Swagger UI, versioned endpoints and deprecation tracking. Docs also say traces can be filtered, exported, shared and compared 'via the UI or API', and SDKs exist in four languages. However, nothing documents complete UI-to-API parity across every feature (dashboards, alerts, annotation queues, Engine), so 'everything' is only implied. The 404s on docs.langchain.com OpenAPI paths are not a contradiction, because the spec is served at the API host. Missing for 10: an explicit UI/API parity statement, per-feature API coverage evidence for dashboards, alerts, annotation queues and Engine, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The LangSmith API is used to programmatically create and manage LangSmith resources
Filter, export, share, and compare traces via the UI or API.
The API host itself serves an interactive Swagger UI
integrate LangSmith with any agent stack using our Python, Typescript, Go, or Java SDKs
